source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.
historical_synonyms_documented: Vitis candicans Engelm. ex A. Gray

morphology_documented.leaves: Rounded cordate to triangular-ovate blades, variably unlobed or deeply lobed, upper surface dark green and becoming glabrous, underside densely felted
morphology_documented.fruit: Berries 15–20 mm diameter, purple-black or pale, without glaucous bloom; skin may be intensely acrid
morphology_documented.habitat: Stream bottoms, thickets, fence lines, disturbed land, often sandy

source_scope_note: Historical varieties and synonyms preserved by original names; measurements never automatically transferred to different modern taxon concepts.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: 1999 flora brackets old name V. candicans; keep in original taxon crosswalk
Fruit taste is a historical observation, not a recommendation to consume unknown grape material
preservation: Additive source record; existing gallery, pictures, credits and species files unchanged
